result.title: AgentFaultBench: State-Verified Evaluation of Tool-Fault Recovery
result.comment: 63 pages, 7 figures, including appendices. Submitted to the NAACL 2027 Industry Track
result.summary: Does recovery advice help an agent finish a task after a tool fails? AgentFaultBench evaluates LangGraph and CrewAI agents performing specified tasks in an isolated GitLab installation. We inject tool errors and check both the resulting files and issues and the required reads, verification and final response. The prompt supplies the expected issue and report text, so the task tests execution rather than content generation. In the primary comparison of 1,944 planned runs, advice changes success by -8.33, 0.00 and +1.06 percentage points relative to a neutral reminder; missing outcomes leave the latter two comparisons inconclusive. Later experiments test a revised recovery policy. GPT-4o mini improves, while Sol and Claude already complete the recoverable cases. In a separate 624-run study on six related tasks not previously used by that policy, the guided condition records 161 correct final states and one unknown outcome in 192 planned runs, versus 142/192 with neutral feedback. The gain lies between +9.90 and +10.42 pp when missing outcomes are included. Removing issue IDs gives 47/48 successes versus 46/48 with IDs; other execution information remains. A second checker agrees on 1,879 observed primary outcomes and 241 constructed test cases. No human validation was collected. The findings support testing advice against explicit recovery controls rather than assuming it helps.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 AgentFaultBench：在隔离 GitLab 环境中向 LangGraph/CrewAI agent 注入工具错误，并用文件、issue 及必需的读取与验证步骤做状态校验，以对照实验检验「恢复建议」是否真的提升任务成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「显式对照条件 + 中间状态校验」的评估协议可能可供核查 LVR 中类似 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的提示增益是否真实，以及如何验证中间读取和停止动作被实际使用；但研究对象是 agent 工具故障恢复而非视觉推理，需较多核查。
